props.name: cu alloy lining against iron carbonyl
props.statement: The reactor and heat exchanger 4 must have a protective layer of Cu-Zn or Cu-Mn alloy to counter the formation of iron carbonyl compounds; the rest of the high-pressure section and the distillation section can use ordinary steels.

props.name: feo partial oxidation rejected
props.note: the process description is from lit. 2 (Kirk-Othmer)
props.statement: Partial oxidation of hydrocarbons at 30 ata and 450 °C over an FeO catalyst gives organic oxygen compounds, chiefly aldehydes and alcohols; lacking a selective catalyst that favours one product such as methanol, a complicated mixture results that needs extensive distillation, and the methanol yield is low, so this process is not considered.

props.name: high pressure process chosen

props.statement: Methanol can be made from CO + 2 H2 under high pressure (250 ata) and temperature (350 °C) with a ZnO, CrO3 catalyst; the product is easy to purify and, despite the cost of strong compression, this route is economically the most advantageous, so it is chosen.

props.name: inlet and cold gas not in literature
props.statement: The amounts of cold and warm synthesis gas entering the reactor are not given in the literature; the report calculates them from a heat balance over the reactor (cold 870 kmol/h, warm 4812 kmol/h).

props.name: low temperature high pressure
props.statement: The value of the equilibrium constant shows that the reaction must take place at as low a temperature as possible; as in ammonia synthesis the temperature cannot be too low because the reaction rate then becomes too small. Raising the pressure favours methanol formation, as the reaction equation shows.

props.name: methanation dominates at 1 ata
props.statement: The calculation at 1 ata shows that the side reaction (CO + 3 H2 -> CH4 + H2O) dominates methanol formation thermodynamically; to make the methanol yield larger than the methane yield, equilibrium 1 must establish much faster than equilibrium 2, which a good catalyst can achieve.

props.name: synthesis gas raw materials
props.statement: The raw materials for making the CO and H2 are coal (producer gas, water gas) or refinery gas (conversion with steam); the Ruhr area or the island of Rozenburg would therefore be suitable plant locations.

props.name: zno cro3 best in patents
props.note: cited from the patent literature (German patents 594.968, 612.229, 490.248, 675.658, 587.818) and lit. 9
props.statement: The patent literature (lit. 4-8) describes many catalysts of varying composition; the best results are obtained with a ZnO, CrO3 catalyst, which is therefore used: 2 parts by weight ZnO to 1 part CrO3, pressed with some graphite and water into cylinders of 10 mm diameter and 10 mm height (lit. 9).
